newsitem.title: USA: Black Americans say racism persists in U.S. military.
newsitem.headline: Black Americans say racism persists in U.S. military.

text.p: African Americans face racial discrimination in all four branches of the armed forces despite government claims to the contrary, black military personnel said Thursday at the NAACP's national conference.
While the Pentagon says the military provides blacks with more opportunities than other sectors of society, panellists said a hidden double standard exists in the armed forces.
Black military personnel, both male and female, told the NAACP they had been subjected to harassment and discrimination during their military careers.
NAACP lawyers plan to publish a report on racism in the military based on their testimony.
William E. Leftwich III, Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defence, said the military "is not immune to problems."

"We have found there is some form of discrimination and sexual harassment that exists," he told the NAACP. He said, however, that the military had made more progress than any other social sector in providing opportunities for blacks.
Leftwich said nearly 30 percent of U.S. military personnel were black and there are more than 50 top-ranking African American officers.
But he said studies have shown that blacks are more likely to be court martialed than whites for similar offences.
The panel was the last in a series of debates held this week on issues affecting minorities at the conference of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People.

Among those testifying was Lt. Crista Davis who said she faced "racism and sexism" during her Air Force career. Davis became pregnant last year in a relationship with a married Air Force major. She said she did not know he was married.
"I'm facing a court martial and criminal charges. He was reprimanded for adultery and basically got off scot free."
The NAACP also heard testimony by Sgt. 1st Class Tony Cross, one of 12 drill sergeants from the Aberdeen army training base in Maryland charged with sexual misconduct.

Cross, charged with consensual sodomy and adultery for allegedly having sex with a white female trainee, said the charges were false and proof of the military's double standard that punishes blacks while treating whites with leniency.
"There is a double standard," he said. "I know I'll be found guilty. You cannot get a fair trial in the military."
